public override func update(_ currentTime: TimeInterval) {\n   334→        let deltaTime = lastUpdateTime == 0 ? 0 : currentTime - lastUpdateTime\n   335→        lastUpdateTime = currentTime\n   336→\n   337→        // Skip updates if game is paused\n   338→        if hud.isGamePaused {\n   339→            showPauseOverlay()\n   340→            return\n   341→        } else {\n   342→            hidePauseOverlay()\n   343→        }\n   344→\n   345→        // Apply game speed multiplier\n   346→        let adjustedDeltaTime = deltaTime * TimeInterval(hud.gameSpeed)\n   347→\n   348→        // Update ability manager cooldowns\n   349→        abilityManager.update(deltaTime: deltaTime)\n   350→\n   351→        switch gameState.currentState {\n   352→        case .building:\n   353→            updateBuildingPhase(deltaTime: adjustedDeltaTime)\n   354→        case .wave:\n   355→            updateWavePhase(deltaTime: adjustedDeltaTime)\n   356→        case .gameOver:\n   357→            handleGameOver()\n   358→        case .victory:\n   359→            handleVictory()\n   360→        default:\n   361→            break\n   362→        }\n   363→    }\n   364→\n   365→    private func updateBuildingPhase(deltaTime: TimeInterval) {\n   366→        buildPhaseTimer += deltaTime\n   367→\n   368→        // Use shorter delay if auto-start is enabled (3 seconds), otherwise use full time (20 seconds)\n   369→        let autoStartDelay: TimeInterval = 3.0\n   370→        let waveStartTime = hud.isAutoStartEnabled ? autoStartDelay : GameConfiguration.timeBetweenWaves\n   371→\n   372→        let timeRemaining = max(0, waveStartTime - buildPhaseTimer)\n   373→        hud.updateBuildTimer(timeRemaining)\n   374→\n   375→        // Auto-start wave if timer expires\n   376→        if buildPhaseTimer >= waveStartTime {\n   377→            startWave()\n   378→        }\n   379→\n   380→        // Apply auto-repair\n   381→        applyAutoRepair(deltaTime: deltaTime)\n   382→    }\n   383→\n   384→    private func updateWavePhase(deltaTime: TimeInterval) {\n   385→        // Update wave manager\n   386→        waveManager.update(deltaTime: deltaTime, activeBugs: bugs.count)\n   387→\n   388→        // Update bugs\n   389→        var bugsToRemove: [Bug] = []\n   390→        for bug in bugs {\n   391→            bug.update(deltaTime: deltaTime, pathfindingGrid: pathfindingGrid)\n   392→\n   393→            // Check if bug reached house\n   394→            if bug.hasReachedHouse() {\n   395→                print(\"💥 Bug reached house! Dealing \\(bug.damage) damage\")\n   396→                gameState.damageHouse(bug.damage)\n   397→                house.takeDamage(bug.damage)\n   398→                bugsToRemove.append(bug)\n   399→            }\n   400→        }\n   401→\n   402→        // Remove bugs that reached house\n   403→        for bug in bugsToRemove {\n   404→            removeBug(bug)\n   405→        }\n   406→\n   407→        // Update structures\n   408→        for structure in structures {\n   409→            structure.update(deltaTime: deltaTime, bugs: bugs)\n   410→        }\n   411→\n   412→        // Update hero\n   413→        hero.update(deltaTime: deltaTime, bugs: bugs)\n   414→\n   415→        // Apply auto-repair during wave\n   416→        applyAutoRepair(deltaTime: deltaTime)\n   417→\n   418→        // Remove dead bugs\n   419→        let deadBugs = bugs.filter { $0.currentHealth <= 0 }\n   420→        for bug in deadBugs {\n   421→            handleBugDeath(bug)\n   422→        }\n   423→    }\n   424→\n   425→    private func applyAutoRepair(deltaTime: TimeInterval) {\n   426→        let totalRepairRate = upgradeManager.totalRepairRate + cardManager.getTotalRepairRate()\n   427→        let repairAmount = Int(CGFloat(totalRepairRate) * CGFloat(deltaTime))\n   428→        if repairAmount > 0 {\n   429→            for structure in structures {\n   430→                structure.repair(repairAmount)\n   431→            }\n   432→        }\n   433→    }\n   434→\n   435→    // MARK: - Wave Management\n   436→\n   437→    public func startWave() {\n   438→ gameState.isBossWave() {\n   463→            if let card = cardManager.awardRandomCard() {\n   464→                showCardRewardPopup(card)\n   465→            }\n   466→        }\n   467→\n   468→        // Award hero power-up every 5 waves\n   469→        if gameState.currentWave % 5 == 0 {\n   470→            hero.awardPowerUp()\n   471→            hud.refreshPowerUpButton()\n   472→        }\n The current algorithm infers segment direction from grid coordinate deltas and then locks axes in world coordinates, causing visible position snaps when bugs are slightly off-path or rounding corners. The fix requires replacing the segment-type detection with simple vector-based movement that always moves directly toward the target waypoint, following the proven pattern from `Hero.swift:110-127`.\n\n## Current Algorithm Analysis\n\n### Algorithm Flow (`Bug.swift:254-316`)\n\nThe bug movement system follows this sequence every frame:\n\n```\n1. Guard check: pathIndex < movementPath.count (line 255)\n   └─ Exit early if path is complete\n\n2. Branch based on grid deltas:\n\n      IF deltaX > 0 AND deltaY > 0 (line 298):\n         → DIAGONAL branch\n         normalizedDx = dx / distance\n         normalizedDy = dy / distance\n         position.x += normalizedDx * moveDistance\n         position.y += normalizedDy * moveDistance\n\n      ELSE IF deltaX > deltaY (line 304):\n         → HORIZONTAL branch\n         moveX = min(abs(dx), moveDistance) * (dx > 0 ? 1 : -1)\n         position.x += moveX\n         position.y = targetWorldPos.y  // ⚠️ AXIS LOCK - SNAP Y COORDINATE\n\n      ELSE (line 309):\n         → VERTICAL branch\n         moveY = min(abs(dy), moveDistance) * (dy > 0 ? 1 : -1)\n         position.y += moveY\n         position.x = targetWorldPos.x  // ⚠️ AXIS LOCK - SNAP X COORDINATE\n```\n\n### Key Variables Involved\n\nFrom `Bug.swift:127-135`:\n- `position: CGPoint` - World coordinates of bug sprite (e.g., x: 120.0, y: 180.0)\n- `gridPosition: GridPosition` - Current grid tile (e.g., GridPosition(3, 4))\n- `movementPath: [GridPosition]` - Array of waypoints from spawn to house\n- `pathIndex: Int` - Index of current target waypoint in movementPath\n- `moveSpeed: CGFloat` - Base speed from bug type (e.g., ant=60, wasp=120)\n- `slowFactor: CGFloat` - Multiplier from traps/cards (default 1.0, can be <1.0 for slowed bugs)\n\n### Movement Branches Detailed\n\n#### Diagonal Branch (Lines 298-303) - CORRECT\n```swift\nif deltaX > 0 && deltaY > 0 {\n    let normalizedDx = dx / distance\n    let normalizedDy = dy / distance\n    position.x += normalizedDx * moveDistance\n    position.y += normalizedDy * moveDistance\n}\n```\n**What it does:** Uses normalized direction vector to move proportionally in both X and Y.\n**Why it's correct:** Always moves directly toward target, no axis assumptions.\n**Problem:** Only triggers when BOTH grid deltas are non-zero. Misses cases where bug needs to correct position errors or is between waypoints.\n\n#### Horizontal Branch (Lines 304-308) - FLAWED\n```swift\nelse if deltaX > deltaY {\n    let moveX = min(abs(dx), moveDistance) * (dx > 0 ? 1 : -1)\n    position.x += moveX\n    position.y = targetWorldPos.y  // ⚠️ SNAP!\n}\n```\n**What it does:** Assumes segment is horizontal, locks Y axis to target, moves only in X.\n**Why it's flawed:** Snaps Y coordinate immediately, assuming bug is already aligned horizontally.\n**When it breaks:** When bug's current position has Y ≠ targetWorldPos.y (common during corner turns).\n\n#### Vertical Branch (Lines 309-314) - FLAWED\n```swift\nelse {\n    let moveY = min(abs(dy), moveDistance) * (dy > 0 ? 1 : -1)\n    position.y += moveY\n    position.x = targetWorldPos.x  // ⚠️ SNAP!\n}\n```\n**What it does:** Assumes segment is vertical, locks X axis to target, moves only in Y.\n**Why it's flawed:** Snaps X coordinate immediately, assuming bug is already aligned vertically.\n**When it breaks:** When bug's current position has X ≠ targetWorldPos.x (common during corner turns).\n\n## Root Cause: Axis-Locking Heuristic Flaw\n\n### The Fundamental Problem\n\nThe algorithm uses **grid coordinate deltas** between waypoints to infer segment type (horizontal/vertical/diagonal), then applies **world coordinate axis locks** based on that inference. This creates a **geometric mismatch** between the decision criteria and the action taken.\n\n**The Core Issue:**\n- **Decision:** Based on `abs(targetGridPos.x - prevGridPos.x)` vs `abs(targetGridPos.y - prevGridPos.y)` (GRID SPACE)\n- **Action:** Locks `position.x` or `position.y` (WORLD SPACE)\n- **Assumption:** Bug is already aligned with the inferred axis\n- **Reality:** Bug position might not be aligned due to overshooting, position errors, or corner transitions\n\n### Concrete Failure Example\n\n**Scenario: Bug rounding a corner from horizontal to vertical segment**\n\n```\nPath waypoints: [(1,3), (2,3), (3,3), (3,4), (3,5)]\n                 start   →→→→→   corner  ↑↑↑   end\n\nCurrent state:\n  Bug world position: (118.0, 140.0)  // Slightly off due to previous frame\n  Bug grid position: (2, 3)\n  pathIndex: 3  // Targeting waypoint (3,4)\n\nTarget waypoint: GridPosition(3, 4)\nTarget world position: (140.0, 180.0)\n\nPrevious waypoint: movementPath[2] = GridPosition(3, 3)\n\nGrid deltas:\n  deltaX = abs(3 - 3) = 0\n  deltaY = abs(4 - 3) = 1\n\nBranch selected: deltaX < deltaY → VERTICAL branch (lines 309-314)\n\nVertical branch executes:\n  position.x = targetWorldPos.x = 140.0  // ⚠️ INSTANT SNAP from 118.0 → 140.0!\n  position.y += moveY  // Normal movement\n\nVisual result: Bug \"pops\" 22 pixels to the right instantly, then moves up.\n              This is visible as drifting off the path or cutting corners.\n```\n\n### Why This Approach Fails Geometrically\n\n**Grid deltas tell us:** The direction from the previous waypoint to the target waypoint.\n\n**Grid deltas DO NOT tell us:** The direction from the bug's CURRENT position to the target waypoint.\n\n**The axis lock assumes:** Bug is already on the segment's primary axis (e.g., Y aligned for horizontal movement).\n\n**This assumption breaks when:**\n1. Bug overshoots a waypoint slightly (deltaTime * high speed > remaining distance)\n2. Bug has accumulated tiny position errors from floating-point arithmetic\n3. Bug is transitioning from one segment type to another (corners)\n4. Bug was slowed/sped during previous frame, affecting position\n\n**Mathematical explanation:**\n\nCurrent approach:\n```\nif (gridDelta_x > gridDelta_y):\n    lock position.y = target.y  // Assumes bug.y already equals target.y\n    move position.x toward target.x\n```\n\nThis is geometrically incorrect when `bug.position.y ≠ target.y`, which is common.\n\nCorrect approach:\n```\ndirection = normalize(target - bug.position)  // Direction from CURRENT position\nbug.position += direction * speed * dt        // Move toward target\n```\n\nThis always moves directly toward the target, regardless of segment orientation.\n\n## Failure Modes\n\n### 1. Curved Paths (Horizontal → Vertical Turns)\n\n**When:** Bug approaches a corner waypoint (e.g., Map 1 \"Winding Road\", Map 8 \"U-Turns\")\n\n**What happens:**\n- Bug moves horizontally with Y-axis locked\n- Reaches corner waypoint, pathIndex increments\n- Next segment is vertical, X-axis gets locked\n- **SNAP:** X position instantly jumps to target X coordinate\n- Bug appears to \"cut the corner\" or drift off the brown road tiles\n\n**Severity:** HIGH - Most visible on maps with many turns (Map 1, Map 8)\n\n**Example trace:**\n```\nFrame N:   position=(118, 120), target=(140, 120) [horizontal segment]\n           → Y locked to 120, move X toward 140\nFrame N+1: position=(138, 120), target=(140, 120)\n           → Distance < 2, snap to (140, 120), pathIndex++\nFrame N+2: position=(140, 120), target=(140, 160) [vertical segment]\n           → X locked to 140 ✓ (already aligned, no snap)\n\nBUT if bug was slightly off:\nFrame N+1: position=(141, 119), target=(140, 120) [overshooting case]\n           → Distance < 2, snap to (140, 120), pathIndex++\nFrame N+2: position=(140, 120), target=(140, 160) [vertical segment]\n           → X locked to 140 ✓ (snap fixed it)\n\nREAL FAILURE CASE:\nFrame N:   position=(138, 122), target=(140, 120) [was off by 2 in Y]\nFrame N+1: position=(139.5, 120), target=(140, 120) [Y snapped but X didn't reach]\nFrame N+2: position=(140, 120), target=(140, 160) [got lucky, snap aligned it]\n\nWORSE CASE:\nFrame N:   position=(137, 122), target=(140, 120)\n           → Horizontal branch: Y snaps to 120 ✓, X moves toward 140\nFrame N+1: position=(139, 120), target=(140, 120)\n           → Still moving, but now aligned\nFrame N+2: position=(140, 120), target=(140, 160)\n           → Vertical branch: X locks to 140 ✓\n\nThe issue: If bug doesn't complete the horizontal segment in one frame,\n          the Y snap happens BEFORE bug reaches the corner waypoint.\n          Bug visually \"slides\" onto the horizontal line instead of\n          following a smooth curve.\n```\n\n### 2. High-Speed Bugs Overshooting Waypoints\n\n**When:** Fast bugs (spider=100, wasp=120) or wave-scaled speeds during high deltaTime frames\n\n**What happens:**\n- Bug approaches waypoint with high `moveDistance = speed * slowFactor * deltaTime`\n- `distance < 2` check (line 280) triggers snap to exact waypoint ✓ (This works)\n- **BUT:** If bug was off-path before snap, the axis lock on PREVIOUS frames caused visible drift\n- Snap logic FIXES the position at waypoints but doesn't prevent drift BETWEEN waypoints\n\n**Severity:** MEDIUM - Drift is less visible for fast bugs (they move quickly), but accumulates over multiple waypoints\n\n**Why axis locks make this worse:**\n- Fast bug moves 5-10 pixels per frame\n- Axis lock snaps perpendicular axis immediately\n- If bug was off by 3 pixels, snap is visible as a \"jerk\"\n- Multiple snaps create stuttering visual effect\n\n### 3. Diagonal Segments (Map 15 \"Diagonal\")\n\n**When:** Path includes diagonal tiles where both X and Y change: `[(2,12), (3,11), (4,10), (5,9)]`\n\n**What happens:**\n- Grid deltas: `deltaX = 1`, `deltaY = 1`\n- Diagonal branch triggers (line 298) ✓ - Uses normalization, so this actually WORKS\n- **No issue here!** The diagonal branch is geometrically correct.\n\n**Severity:** NONE for pure diagonal segments\n\n**However:** Mixed diagonal-orthogonal paths can still fail:\n```\nPath: [(2,12), (3,11), (4,10), (5,10), (6,10)]  // Diagonal then horizontal\n\nAt waypoint (4,10) → (5,10):\n  deltaX = 1, deltaY = 0 → Horizontal branch\n  Y axis locked → If bug is slightly off in Y, SNAP occurs\n```\n\n### 4. Segment-Type Detection Logic Flaw\n\n**When:** Always - the logic itself is flawed, not just edge cases\n\n**The problem:** Branch selection based on grid deltas doesn't account for:\n\n1. **Bug between waypoints:** When bug is at world position (135, 145) but gridPosition is (3,3) and targeting (3,4):\n   - `prevGridPos = gridPosition = (3,3)` (line 293)\n   - `targetGridPos = (3,4)`\n   - `deltaX = 0, deltaY = 1` → Vertical branch\n   - But bug might not be aligned at X=140 yet! Snap occurs.\n\n2. **Position error accumulation:** Floating-point errors or previous frame's slowFactor changes:\n   - Bug should be at (140, 160) but is at (139.8, 160.1)\n   - On next waypoint, axis lock snaps to new coordinate\n   - Small errors accumulate into visible drift\n\n3. **Frame timing variance:** Different deltaTime values between frames:\n   - Frame 1: deltaTime=0.016 → moves 6 pixels\n   - Frame 2: deltaTime=0.020 → moves 7.5 pixels\n   - Inconsistent progress can cause bug to be off-axis when branch changes\n\n**Severity:** HIGH - This is the root cause affecting all other failure modes\n\n## Path System Verification\n\n### expandPath() Analysis (`MapConfiguration.swift:71-103`)\n\n**Algorithm:**\n```swift\nprivate static func expandPath(_ waypoints: [GridPosition]) -> [GridPosition] {\n    guard waypoints.count >= 2 else { return waypoints }\n    var expandedPath: [GridPosition] = [waypoints[0]]\n\n    for i in 1..<waypoints.count {\n        let start = waypoints[i - 1]\n        let end = waypoints[i]\n        let dx = end.x - start.x\n        let dy = end.y - start.y\n        let steps = max(abs(dx), abs(dy))  // ✓ Correctly handles orthogonal AND diagonal\n\n        if steps == 0 { continue }\n\n        for step in 1...steps {\n            let x = start.x + (dx * step) / steps  // ✓ Linear interpolation\n            let y = start.y + (dy * step) / steps\n            let position = GridPosition(x: x, y: y)\n            if position != expandedPath.last {\n                expandedPath.append(position)\n            }\n        }\n    }\n    return expandedPath\n}\n```\n\n**Verification Results:**\n\n✅ **Path expansion is CORRECT**\n- Uses `max(abs(dx), abs(dy))` to calculate steps → Handles both orthogonal and diagonal segments\n- Linear interpolation fills ALL intermediate tiles → No gaps possible\n- Duplicate prevention ensures clean path array\n- Works for horizontal: `steps = max(5, 0) = 5` → 5 intermediate tiles\n- Works for vertical: `steps = max(0, 4) = 4` → 4 intermediate tiles\n- Works for diagonal: `steps = max(3, 3) = 3` → 3 intermediate tiles\n\n**Tested mentally with Map 1 (Winding Road):**\n- Sparse waypoints: `[(1,1), (5,1), (5,5), (10,5)]`\n- Expansion: `[(1,1), (2,1), (3,1), (4,1), (5,1), (5,2), (5,3), (5,4), (5,5), (6,5), (7,5), (8,5), (9,5), (10,5)]`\n- Every tile included ✓\n\n**Tested mentally with Map 15 (Diagonal):**\n- Diagonal segment: `[(2,12), (5,9)]`\n- `dx=3, dy=-3, steps=max(3,3)=3`\n- Expansion: `[(2,12), (3,11), (4,10), (5,9)]`\n- All diagonal tiles included ✓\n\n**Conclusion:** The movement drift is NOT caused by path definition. Paths are geometrically correct and complete. The issue is purely in the movement algorithm (`Bug.swift:292-314`).\n\n## Geometric Analysis of Position Drift\n\n### Mathematical Explanation\n\n**Current approach (FLAWED):**\n```\nsegmentType = inferFromGridDeltas(prevWaypoint, targetWaypoint)\nif segmentType == HORIZONTAL:\n    lock bug.position.y = target.y  // Assumes bug.y already equals target.y\n    move bug.position.x toward target.x\n```\n\n**Why this fails mathematically:**\n\nGiven:\n- Bug current position: `P = (Px, Py)` in world coordinates\n- Target waypoint: `T = (Tx, Ty)` in world coordinates\n- Previous waypoint: `Pprev` in grid coordinates (not world!)\n\nThe algorithm:\n1. Calculates `gridDelta = targetGrid - prevGrid` (in GRID SPACE)\n2. Infers segment orientation from `gridDelta`\n3. Applies axis lock to `P` (in WORLD SPACE)\n\n**The mismatch:**\n- `gridDelta` describes the path segment from `Pprev` to `T`\n- But `P` is the bug's CURRENT position, which may not lie on the line from `Pprev` to `T`\n- Locking an axis forces `P` onto the line, but does so instantly (snap), not smoothly\n\n**Example of geometric incorrectness:**\n\n```\nPprev = GridPosition(2, 3) → world (100, 140)\nT = GridPosition(3, 3) → world (140, 140)\nP_current = (118, 142)  // Bug is 2 pixels above the line\n\ngridDelta = (1, 0) → horizontal segment detected\nAxis lock: P.y = T.y = 140  // SNAP from 142 → 140\nResult: Bug visibly \"drops\" 2 pixels instantly\n```\n\n**Correct approach (SMOOTH):**\n\n```\ndirection = normalize(T - P)  // Direction from current position to target\nP += direction * speed * deltaTime  // Move toward target smoothly\n```\n\nUsing the same example:\n```\nP_current = (118, 142)\nT = (140, 140)\ndelta = T - P = (22, -2)\ndistance = sqrt(22² + 2²) = sqrt(488) ≈ 22.09\ndirection = (22/22.09, -2/22.09) ≈ (0.995, -0.091)\n\nIf speed * deltaTime = 5:\nP_next = P + direction * 5 = (118 + 4.975, 142 - 0.455) = (122.975, 141.545)\n\nNext frame:\ndelta = (140, 140) - (122.975, 141.545) = (17.025, -1.545)\ndistance ≈ 17.09\ndirection ≈ (0.996, -0.090)\nP_next = (122.975 + 4.98, 141.545 - 0.45) = (127.955, 141.095)\n\n... bug smoothly moves toward (140, 140) in both X and Y simultaneously\n```\n\n**Key insight:** The correct approach calculates direction from CURRENT position, not from previous waypoint. This ensures smooth movement even when bug is off-path.\n\n### Why Axis Locks Fail on Curves\n\n**At a corner waypoint:**\n\n```\nPath: [..., (2,3), (3,3), (3,4), ...]\n                  corner\n\nBug approaching (3,3) horizontally from (2,3):\n  - Horizontal branch active: Y locked to 140 (y-coordinate of row 3)\n  - Bug reaches (3,3), pathIndex increments to target (3,4)\n\nBug now targeting (3,4) vertically:\n  - Vertical branch activates: X locked to 140 (x-coordinate of column 3)\n  - IF bug.x was already 140 → smooth transition ✓\n  - IF bug.x was 139.5 due to timing → SNAP to 140 ✗ (visible jerk)\n```\n\n**The problem at corners:**\n- Axis locks ASSUME perfect alignment at waypoint arrival\n- The `distance < 2` check snaps position (line 282), which should fix this\n- **BUT:** If bug doesn't trigger the snap (e.g., approaches waypoint at an angle due to previous drift), the axis lock on the NEW segment snaps BEFORE the waypoint is reached\n\n**Real-world corner scenario:**\n\n```\nFrame N-2: Bug at (136, 138), target (140, 140) [horizontal segment]\n           distance = 5.66, no snap, horizontal branch\n           Y locked to 140 → position becomes (136, 140) [SNAP!]\n           X moves toward 140 → position becomes (138, 140)\n\nFrame N-1: Bug at (138, 140), target (140, 140)\n           distance = 2, no snap yet (≥ 2)\n           Horizontal branch: Y=140 ✓, X moves → (140, 140)\n\nFrame N:   Bug at (140, 140), target (140, 140)\n           distance = 0 < 2 → SNAP to (140, 140), pathIndex++\n\nFrame N+1: Bug at (140, 140), target (140, 180) [vertical segment]\n           distance = 40\n           Vertical branch: X locked to 140 ✓ (already aligned)\n           Y moves toward 180 → (140, 142)\n```\n\nIn this scenario, the system worked because the snap happened before the corner. But if Frame N-2 had bug at (136, 141) instead of (136, 138):\n\n```\nFrame N-2: Bug at (136, 141), target (140, 140)\n           Horizontal branch: Y locked to 140 → (136, 140) [SNAP from 141!]\n```\n\nThe snap is visible as a 1-pixel \"jerk\" downward. Multiple such snaps across a path create the \"drifting off road\" visual effect.\n\n## Recommended Solution\n\n### Vector-Based Movement (Hero.swift Pattern)\n\n**Replace lines 292-314 with:**\n\n```swift\n// Calculate direction and move toward target\nlet moveDistance = moveSpeed * slowFactor * CGFloat(deltaTime)\n\n// Always move directly toward target using normalized direction\n// (Following pattern from Hero.swift:110-127)\nlet ratio = min(1.0, moveDistance / distance)\nposition.x += dx * ratio\nposition.y += dy * ratio\n\n// Note: gridPosition will be updated when waypoint is reached (line 283)\n```\n\n### Why This Approach Is Correct\n\n**1. Geometric correctness:**\n- Direction vector `(dx, dy)` points from current position to target\n- Normalization via `ratio = moveDistance / distance` ensures speed is constant\n- Bug ALWAYS moves directly toward target, regardless of path shape\n\n**2. Handles all path types:**\n- Horizontal segments: `dy ≈ 0`, so `ratio * dy ≈ 0`, Y changes minimally ✓\n- Vertical segments: `dx ≈ 0`, so `ratio * dx ≈ 0`, X changes minimally ✓\n- Diagonal segments: Both `dx` and `dy` non-zero, both update proportionally ✓\n- Curved paths: Direction recalculates each frame based on CURRENT position ✓\n\n**3. No axis assumptions:**\n- Never assumes bug is already aligned with any axis\n- Works even if bug is off-path due to previous errors\n- Naturally corrects position errors over time\n\n**4. Mathematical equivalence to normalization:**\n\nThe ratio approach: `position += delta * (moveDistance / distance)`\n\nIs equivalent to: `position += normalize(delta) * moveDistance`\n\nBecause: `normalize(delta) = delta / distance`\n\nTherefore: `delta * (moveDistance / distance) = normalize(delta) * moveDistance` ✓\n\n**5. Proven pattern:**\n\nFrom `Hero.swift:110-127`:\n```swift\nlet dx = targetWorldPos.x - position.x\nlet dy = targetWorldPos.y - position.y\nlet distance = sqrt(dx * dx + dy * dy)\n\nif distance < 5.0 {\n    position = targetWorldPos\n    currentGridPosition = target\n    targetPosition = nil\n} else {\n    let moveDistance = moveSpeed * CGFloat(deltaTime)\n    let ratio = min(1.0, moveDistance / distance)\n    position.x += dx * ratio\n    position.y += dy * ratio\n}\n```\n\nHero movement is smooth and doesn't drift. Same logic should apply to bugs.\n\n### What to Preserve\n\n**Keep unchanged:**\n- Lines 255-270: Guard check and burrowing logic (unrelated to drift)\n- Lines 272-278: Target waypoint and distance calculation (correct)\n- Lines 280-285: Waypoint snap logic (prevents division by zero, ensures exact positioning at waypoints)\n\n**Remove entirely:**\n- Lines 292-296: Segment direction detection from grid deltas\n- Lines 297-314: Three-branch movement logic (diagonal/horizontal/vertical)\n\n**Result:** Simpler, more maintainable code that is geometrically correct.\n\n### Performance Considerations\n\n**Computational complexity:** O(1) per frame per bug (same as current)\n\n**Operations comparison:**\n\nCurrent approach:\n- 2x grid position lookups\n- 2x abs() calls (deltaX, deltaY)\n- 2-3 comparisons for branching\n- 1x sqrt() for distance\n- 2-3 arithmetic operations per branch\n- **Total: ~10-12 operations**\n\nProposed approach:\n- 1x sqrt() for distance\n- 3x divisions (ratio calculation, implicit in multiplication)\n- 2x additions for position update\n- **Total: ~6 operations**\n\n**Proposed approach is actually SIMPLER and potentially faster!**\n\nNo performance concerns. The sqrt() call was already present (line 278), so no new overhead.\n\n## Test Scenarios for Implementation (TASK1)\n\n### Unit Tests (Tests/BugDefenseTests/)\n\n**Test framework:** XCTest\n**Test command:** `swift test`\n**Pattern:** Follow `BugDefenseTests.swift:1-100` for structure\n\n#### 1. Straight Horizontal Path Test\n```swift\n@MainActor\nfunc testBugMovementHorizontalPath() {\n    // Given: Bug with horizontal path\n    let bug = Bug(type: .ant, health: 20, damage: 5, difficulty: 1.0)\n    let path: [GridPosition] = [\n        GridPosition(x: 1, y: 5),\n        GridPosition(x: 2, y: 5),\n        GridPosition(x: 3, y: 5),\n        GridPosition(x: 4, y: 5),\n        GridPosition(x: 5, y: 5)\n    ]\n    bug.setPath(path)\n\n    let initialY = bug.position.y\n\n    // When: Update multiple times\n    for _ in 0..<20 {\n        bug.update(deltaTime: 0.016, pathfindingGrid: PathfindingGrid())\n    }\n\n    // Then: Y coordinate remains constant (within tolerance)\n    XCTAssertEqual(bug.position.y, initialY, accuracy: 1.0)\n\n    // And: Bug progresses in X direction\n    XCTAssertGreaterThan(bug.position.x, path[0].toWorldPosition().x)\n}\n```\n\n#### 2. Straight Vertical Path Test\n```swift\n@MainActor\nfunc testBugMovementVerticalPath() {\n    // Given: Bug with vertical path\n    let bug = Bug(type: .ant, health: 20, damage: 5, difficulty: 1.0)\n    let path: [GridPosition] = [\n        GridPosition(x: 5, y: 1),\n        GridPosition(x: 5, y: 2),\n        GridPosition(x: 5, y: 3),\n        GridPosition(x: 5, y: 4),\n        GridPosition(x: 5, y: 5)\n    ]\n    bug.setPath(path)\n\n    let initialX = bug.position.x\n\n    // When: Update multiple times\n    for _ in 0..<20 {\n        bug.update(deltaTime: 0.016, pathfindingGrid: PathfindingGrid())\n    }\n\n    // Then: X coordinate remains constant\n    XCTAssertEqual(bug.position.x, initialX, accuracy: 1.0)\n\n    // And: Bug progresses in Y direction\n    XCTAssertGreaterThan(bug.position.y, path[0].toWorldPosition().y)\n}\n```\n\n#### 3. L-Shaped Curved Path Test (CRITICAL)\n```swift\n@MainActor\nfunc testBugMovementCurvedPath() {\n    // Given: Bug with L-shaped path (corner turn)\n    let bug = Bug(type: .ant, health: 20, damage: 5, difficulty: 1.0)\n    let path: [GridPosition] = [\n        GridPosition(x: 1, y: 3),\n        GridPosition(x: 2, y: 3),\n        GridPosition(x: 3, y: 3),  // Corner waypoint\n        GridPosition(x: 3, y: 4),\n        GridPosition(x: 3, y: 5)\n    ]\n    bug.setPath(path)\n\n    var positions: [CGPoint] = []\n\n    // When: Update and record positions\n    for _ in 0..<50 {\n        positions.append(bug.position)\n        bug.update(deltaTime: 0.016, pathfindingGrid: PathfindingGrid())\n    }\n\n    // Then: No sudden position jumps (max delta < 5 pixels per frame)\n    for i in 1..<positions.count {\n        let deltaX = abs(positions[i].x - positions[i-1].x)\n        let deltaY = abs(positions[i].y - positions[i-1].y)\n        XCTAssertLessThan(deltaX, 5.0, \"Sudden X jump at frame \\(i)\")\n        XCTAssertLessThan(deltaY, 5.0, \"Sudden Y jump at frame \\(i)\")\n    }\n\n    // And: Bug reaches the last waypoint\n    XCTAssertEqual(bug.gridPosition, path.last!)\n}\n```\n\n#### 4. Diagonal Path Test\n```swift\n@MainActor\nfunc testBugMovementDiagonalPath() {\n    // Given: Bug with diagonal path (Map 15 style)\n    let bug = Bug(type: .ant, health: 20, damage: 5, difficulty: 1.0)\n    let path: [GridPosition] = [\n        GridPosition(x: 2, y: 12),\n        GridPosition(x: 3, y: 11),\n        GridPosition(x: 4, y: 10),\n        GridPosition(x: 5, y: 9)\n    ]\n    bug.setPath(path)\n\n    // When: Update until bug reaches end\n    for _ in 0..<100 {\n        bug.update(deltaTime: 0.016, pathfindingGrid: PathfindingGrid())\n        if bug.gridPosition == path.last! { break }\n    }\n\n    // Then: Bug reaches last waypoint\n    XCTAssertEqual(bug.gridPosition, path.last!)\n\n    // And: Bug position matches world position of last waypoint\n    XCTAssertEqual(bug.position.x, path.last!.toWorldPosition().x, accuracy: 2.0)\n    XCTAssertEqual(bug.position.y, path.last!.toWorldPosition().y, accuracy: 2.0)\n}\n```\n\n#### 5. 1]\n   240→        let end = waypoints[i]\n   241→        let dx = end.x - start.x\n   242→        let dy = end.y - start.y\n   243→        let steps = max(abs(dx), abs(dy))  // Correctly handles orthogonal and diagonal\n   244→\n   245→        if steps == 0 { continue }\n   246→\n   247→        for step in 1...steps {\n   248→            let x = start.x + (dx * step) / steps  // Linear interpolation\n   249→            let y = start.y + (dy * step) / steps\n   250→            let position = GridPosition(x: x, y: y)\n   251→            if position != expandedPath.last {\n   252→                expandedPath.append(position)\n   253→            }\n   254→        }\n   255→    }\n   256→    return expandedPath\n   257→}\n   258→```\n   259→\n   260→**Verification Result: PATH SYSTEM IS CORRECT**\n   261→\n   262→- Uses `max(abs(dx), abs(dy))` to calculate steps - The current algorithm infers segment direction from grid coordinate deltas and then locks axes in world coordinates, causing visible position snaps when bugs are slightly off-path or rounding corners. The fix requires replacing the segment-type detection with simple vector-based movement that always moves directly toward the target waypoint, following the proven pattern from `Hero.swift:110-127`.\n     6→\n     7→## Current Algorithm Analysis\n     8→\n     9→### Algorithm Flow (`Bug.swift:254-316`)\n    10→\n    11→The bug movement system follows this sequence every frame:\n    12→\n    13→```\n    14→1. 1 : -1)\n    59→         position.y += moveY\n    60→         position.x = targetWorldPos.x  // ⚠️ AXIS LOCK - SNAP X COORDINATE\n    61→```\n    62→\n    63→### Key Variables Involved\n    64→\n    65→From `Bug.swift:127-135`:\n    66→- `position: CGPoint` - World coordinates of bug sprite (e.g., x: 120.0, y: 180.0)\n    67→- `gridPosition: GridPosition` - Current grid tile (e.g., GridPosition(3, 4))\n    68→- `movementPath: [GridPosition]` - Array of waypoints from spawn to house\n    69→- `pathIndex: Int` - Index of current target waypoint in movementPath\n    70→- `moveSpeed: CGFloat` - Base speed from bug type (e.g., ant=60, wasp=120)\n    71→- `slowFactor: CGFloat` - Multiplier from traps/cards (default 1.0, can be <1.0 for slowed bugs)\n    72→\n    73→### Movement Branches Detailed\n    74→\n    75→#### Diagonal Branch (Lines 298-303) - CORRECT\n    76→```swift\n    77→if deltaX > 0 && deltaY > 0 {\n    78→    let normalizedDx = dx / distance\n    79→    let normalizedDy = dy / distance\n    80→    position.x += normalizedDx * moveDistance\n    81→    position.y += normalizedDy * moveDistance\n    82→}\n    83→```\n    84→**What it does:** Uses normalized direction vector to move proportionally in both X and Y.\n    85→**Why it's correct:** Always moves directly toward target, no axis assumptions.\n    86→**Problem:** Only triggers when BOTH grid deltas are non-zero. Misses cases where bug needs to correct position errors or is between waypoints.\n    87→\n    88→#### Horizontal Branch (Lines 304-308) - FLAWED\n    89→```swift\n    90→else if deltaX > deltaY {\n    91→    let moveX = min(abs(dx), moveDistance) * (dx > 0 ? 1 : -1)\n    92→    position.x += moveX\n    93→    position.y = targetWorldPos.y  // ⚠️ SNAP!\n    94→}\n    95→```\n    96→**What it does:** Assumes segment is horizontal, locks Y axis to target, moves only in X.\n    97→**Why it's flawed:** Snaps Y coordinate immediately, assuming bug is already aligned horizontally.\n    98→**When it breaks:** When bug's current position has Y ≠ targetWorldPos.y (common during corner turns).\n    99→\n   100→#### Vertical Branch (Lines 309-314) - FLAWED\n   101→```swift\n   102→else {\n   103→    let moveY = min(abs(dy), moveDistance) * (dy > 0 ? 1 : -1)\n   104→    position.y += moveY\n   105→    position.x = targetWorldPos.x  // ⚠️ SNAP!\n   106→}\n   107→```\n   108→**What it does:** Assumes segment is vertical, locks X axis to target, moves only in Y.\n   109→**Why it's flawed:** Snaps X coordinate immediately, assuming bug is already aligned vertically.\n   110→**When it breaks:** When bug's current position has X ≠ targetWorldPos.x (common during corner turns).\n   111→\n   112→## Root Cause: Axis-Locking Heuristic Flaw\n   113→\n   114→### The Fundamental Problem\n   115→\n   116→The algorithm uses **grid coordinate deltas** between waypoints to infer segment type (horizontal/vertical/diagonal), then applies **world coordinate axis locks** based on that inference. This creates a **geometric mismatch** between the decision criteria and the action taken.\n   117→\n   118→**The Core Issue:**\n   119→- **Decision:** Based on `abs(targetGridPos.x - prevGridPos.x)` vs `abs(targetGridPos.y - prevGridPos.y)` (GRID SPACE)\n   120→- **Action:** Locks `position.x` or `position.y` (WORLD SPACE)\n   121→- **Assumption:** Bug is already aligned with the inferred axis\n   122→- **Reality:** Bug position might not be aligned due to overshooting, position errors, or corner transitions\n   123→\n   124→### Concrete Failure Example\n   125→\n   126→**Scenario: Bug rounding a corner from horizontal to vertical segment**\n   127→\n   128→```\n   129→Path waypoints: [(1,3), (2,3), (3,3), (3,4), (3,5)]\n   130→                 start   →→→→→   corner  ↑↑↑   end\n   131→\n   132→Current state:\n   133→  Bug world position: (118.0, 140.0)  // Slightly off due to previous frame\n   134→  Bug grid position: (2, 3)\n   135→  pathIndex: 3  // Targeting waypoint (3,4)\n   136→\n   137→Target waypoint: GridPosition(3, 4)\n   138→Target world position: (140.0, 180.0)\n   139→\n   140→Previous waypoint: movementPath[2] = GridPosition(3, 3)\n   141→\n   142→Grid deltas:\n   143→  deltaX = abs(3 - 3) = 0\n   144→  deltaY = abs(4 - 3) = 1\n   145→\n   146→Branch selected: deltaX < deltaY → VERTICAL branch (lines 309-314)\n   147→\n   148→Vertical branch executes:\n   149→  position.x = targetWorldPos.x = 140.0  // ⚠️ INSTANT SNAP from 118.0 → 140.0!\n   150→  position.y += moveY  // Normal movement\n   151→\n   152→Visual result: Bug \"pops\" 22 pixels to the right instantly, then moves up.\n   153→              This is visible as drifting off the path or cutting corners.\n   154→```\n   155→\n   156→### Why This Approach Fails Geometrically\n   157→\n   158→**Grid deltas tell us:** The direction from the previous waypoint to the target waypoint.\n   159→\n   160→**Grid deltas DO NOT tell us:** The direction from the bug's CURRENT position to the target waypoint.\n   161→\n   162→**The axis lock assumes:** Bug is already on the segment's primary axis (e.g., Y aligned for horizontal movement).\n   163→\n   164→**This assumption breaks when:**\n   165→1. Bug overshoots a waypoint slightly (deltaTime * high speed > remaining distance)\n   166→2. Bug has accumulated tiny position errors from floating-point arithmetic\n   167→3. Bug is transitioning from one segment type to another (corners)\n   168→4. Bug was slowed/sped during previous frame, affecting position\n   169→\n   170→**Mathematical explanation:**\n   171→\n   172→Current approach:\n   173→```\n   174→if (gridDelta_x > gridDelta_y):\n   175→    lock position.y = target.y  // Assumes bug.y already equals target.y\n   176→    move position.x toward target.x\n   177→```\n   178→\n   179→This is geometrically incorrect when `bug.position.y ≠ target.y`, which is common.\n   180→\n   181→Correct approach:\n   182→```\n   183→direction = normalize(target - bug.position)  // Direction from CURRENT position\n   184→bug.position += direction * speed * dt        // Move toward target\n   185→```\n   186→\n   187→This always moves directly toward the target, regardless of segment orientation.\n   188→\n   189→## Failure Modes\n   190→\n   191→### 1. Curved Paths (Horizontal → Vertical Turns)\n   192→\n   193→**When:** Bug approaches a corner waypoint (e.g., Map 1 \"Winding Road\", Map 8 \"U-Turns\")\n   194→\n   195→**What happens:**\n   196→- Bug moves horizontally with Y-axis locked\n   197→- Reaches corner waypoint, pathIndex increments\n   198→- Next segment is vertical, X-axis gets locked\n   199→- **SNAP:** X position instantly jumps to target X coordinate\n   200→- Bug appears to \"cut the corner\" or drift off the brown road tiles\n   201→\n   202→**Severity:** HIGH - Most visible on maps with many turns (Map 1, Map 8)\n   203→\n   204→**Example trace:**\n   205→```\n   206→Frame N:   position=(118, 120), target=(140, 120) [horizontal segment]\n   207→           → Y locked to 120, move X toward 140\n   208→Frame N+1: position=(138, 120), target=(140, 120)\n   209→           → Distance < 2, snap to (140, 120), pathIndex++\n   210→Frame N+2: position=(140, 120), target=(140, 160) [vertical segment]\n   211→           → X locked to 140 ✓ (already aligned, no snap)\n   212→\n   213→BUT if bug was slightly off:\n   214→Frame N+1: position=(141, 119), target=(140, 120) [overshooting case]\n   215→           → Distance < 2, snap to (140, 120), pathIndex++\n   216→Frame N+2: position=(140, 120), target=(140, 160) [vertical segment]\n   217→           → X locked to 140 ✓ (snap fixed it)\n   218→\n   219→REAL FAILURE CASE:\n   220→Frame N:   position=(138, 122), target=(140, 120) [was off by 2 in Y]\n   221→Frame N+1: position=(139.5, 120), target=(140, 120) [Y snapped but X didn't reach]\n   222→Frame N+2: position=(140, 120), target=(140, 160) [got lucky, snap aligned it]\n   223→\n   224→WORSE CASE:\n   225→Frame N:   position=(137, 122), target=(140, 120)\n   226→           → Horizontal branch: Y snaps to 120 ✓, X moves toward 140\n   227→Frame N+1: position=(139, 120), target=(140, 120)\n   228→           → Still moving, but now aligned\n   229→Frame N+2: position=(140, 120), target=(140, 160)\n   230→           → Vertical branch: X locks to 140 ✓\n   231→\n   232→The issue: If bug doesn't complete the horizontal segment in one frame,\n   233→          the Y snap happens BEFORE bug reaches the corner waypoint.\n   234→          Bug visually \"slides\" onto the horizontal line instead of\n   235→          following a smooth curve.\n   236→```\n   237→\n   238→### 2. High-Speed Bugs Overshooting Waypoints\n   239→\n   240→**When:** Fast bugs (spider=100, wasp=120) or wave-scaled speeds during high deltaTime frames\n   241→\n   242→**What happens:**\n   243→- Bug approaches waypoint with high `moveDistance = speed * slowFactor * deltaTime`\n   244→- `distance < 2` check (line 280) triggers snap to exact waypoint ✓ (This works)\n   245→- **BUT:** If bug was off-path before snap, the axis lock on PREVIOUS frames caused visible drift\n   246→- Snap logic FIXES the position at waypoints but doesn't prevent drift BETWEEN waypoints\n   247→\n   248→**Severity:** MEDIUM - Drift is less visible for fast bugs (they move quickly), but accumulates over multiple waypoints\n   249→\n   250→**Why axis locks make this worse:**\n   251→- Fast bug moves 5-10 pixels per frame\n   252→- Axis lock snaps perpendicular axis immediately\n   253→- If bug was off by 3 pixels, snap is visible as a \"jerk\"\n   254→- Multiple snaps create stuttering visual effect\n   255→\n   256→### 3. Diagonal Segments (Map 15 \"Diagonal\")\n   257→\n   258→**When:** Path includes diagonal tiles where both X and Y change: `[(2,12), (3,11), (4,10), (5,9)]`\n   259→\n   260→**What happens:**\n   261→- Grid deltas: `deltaX = 1`, `deltaY = 1`\n   262→- Diagonal branch triggers (line 298) ✓ - Uses normalization, so this actually WORKS\n   263→- **No issue here!** The diagonal branch is geometrically correct.\n   264→\n   265→**Severity:** NONE for pure diagonal segments\n   266→\n   267→**However:** Mixed diagonal-orthogonal paths can still fail:\n   268→```\n   269→Path: [(2,12), (3,11), (4,10), (5,10), (6,10)]  // Diagonal then horizontal\n   270→\n   271→At waypoint (4,10) → (5,10):\n   272→  deltaX = 1, deltaY = 0 → Horizontal branch\n   273→  Y axis locked → If bug is slightly off in Y, SNAP occurs\n   274→```\n   275→\n   276→### 4. Segment-Type Detection Logic Flaw\n   277→\n   278→**When:** Always - the logic itself is flawed, not just edge cases\n   279→\n   280→**The problem:** Branch selection based on grid deltas doesn't account for:\n   281→\n   282→1. **Bug between waypoints:** When bug is at world position (135, 145) but gridPosition is (3,3) and targeting (3,4):\n   283→   - `prevGridPos = gridPosition = (3,3)` (line 293)\n   284→   - `targetGridPos = (3,4)`\n   285→   - `deltaX = 0, deltaY = 1` → Vertical branch\n   286→   - But bug might not be aligned at X=140 yet! Snap occurs.\n   287→\n   288→2. **Position error accumulation:** Floating-point errors or previous frame's slowFactor changes:\n   289→   - Bug should be at (140, 160) but is at (139.8, 160.1)\n   290→   - On next waypoint, axis lock snaps to new coordinate\n   291→   - Small errors accumulate into visible drift\n   292→\n   293→3. **Frame timing variance:** Different deltaTime values between frames:\n   294→   - Frame 1: deltaTime=0.016 → moves 6 pixels\n   295→   - Frame 2: deltaTime=0.020 → moves 7.5 pixels\n   296→   - Inconsistent progress can cause bug to be off-axis when branch changes\n   297→\n   298→**Severity:** HIGH - This is the root cause affecting all other failure modes\n   299→\n   300→## Path System Verification\n   301→\n   302→### expandPath() Analysis (`MapConfiguration.swift:71-103`)\n   303→\n   304→**Algorithm:**\n   305→```swift\n   306→private static func expandPath(_ waypoints: [GridPosition]) -> [GridPosition] {\n   307→    guard waypoints.count >= 2 else { return waypoints }\n   308→    var expandedPath: [GridPosition] = [waypoints[0]]\n   309→\n   310→    for i in 1..<waypoints.count {\n   311→        let start = waypoints[i - 1]\n   312→        let end = waypoints[i]\n   313→        let dx = end.x - start.x\n   314→        let dy = end.y - start.y\n   315→        let steps = max(abs(dx), abs(dy))  // ✓ Correctly handles orthogonal AND diagonal\n   316→\n   317→        if steps == 0 { continue }\n   318→\n   319→        for step in 1...steps {\n   320→            let x = start.x + (dx * step) / steps  // ✓ Linear interpolation\n   321→            let y = start.y + (dy * step) / steps\n   322→            let position = GridPosition(x: x, y: y)\n   323→            if position != expandedPath.last {\n   324→                expandedPath.append(position)\n   325→            }\n   326→        }\n   327→    }\n   328→    return expandedPath\n   329→}\n   330→```\n   331→\n   332→**Verification Results:**\n   333→\n   334→✅ **Path expansion is CORRECT**\n   335→- Uses `max(abs(dx), abs(dy))` to calculate steps → Handles both orthogonal and diagonal segments\n   336→- Linear interpolation fills ALL intermediate tiles → No gaps possible\n   337→- Duplicate prevention ensures clean path array\n   338→- Works for horizontal: `steps = max(5, 0) = 5` → 5 intermediate tiles\n   339→- Works for vertical: `steps = max(0, 4) = 4` → 4 intermediate tiles\n   340→- Works for diagonal: `steps = max(3, 3) = 3` → 3 intermediate tiles\n   341→\n   342→**Tested mentally with Map 1 (Winding Road):**\n   343→- Sparse waypoints: `[(1,1), (5,1), (5,5), (10,5)]`\n   344→- Expansion: `[(1,1), (2,1), (3,1), (4,1), (5,1), (5,2), (5,3), (5,4), (5,5), (6,5), (7,5), (8,5), (9,5), (10,5)]`\n   345→- Every tile included ✓\n   346→\n   347→**Tested mentally with Map 15 (Diagonal):**\n   348→- Diagonal segment: `[(2,12), (5,9)]`\n   349→- `dx=3, dy=-3, steps=max(3,3)=3`\n   350→- Expansion: `[(2,12), (3,11), (4,10), (5,9)]`\n   351→- All diagonal tiles included ✓\n   352→\n   353→**Conclusion:** The movement drift is NOT caused by path definition. Paths are geometrically correct and complete. The issue is purely in the movement algorithm (`Bug.swift:292-314`).\n   354→\n   355→## Geometric Analysis of Position Drift\n   356→\n   357→### Mathematical Explanation\n   358→\n   359→**Current approach (FLAWED):**\n   360→```\n   361→segmentType = inferFromGridDeltas(prevWaypoint, targetWaypoint)\n   362→if segmentType == HORIZONTAL:\n   363→    lock bug.position.y = target.y  // Assumes bug.y already equals target.y\n   364→    move bug.position.x toward target.x\n   365→```\n   366→\n   367→**Why this fails mathematically:**\n   368→\n   369→Given:\n   370→- Bug current position: `P = (Px, Py)` in world coordinates\n   371→- Target waypoint: `T = (Tx, Ty)` in world coordinates\n   372→- Previous waypoint: `Pprev` in grid coordinates (not world!)\n   373→\n   374→The algorithm:\n   375→1. Calculates `gridDelta = targetGrid - prevGrid` (in GRID SPACE)\n   376→2. Infers segment orientation from `gridDelta`\n   377→3. Applies axis lock to `P` (in WORLD SPACE)\n   378→\n   379→**The mismatch:**\n   380→- `gridDelta` describes the path segment from `Pprev` to `T`\n   381→- But `P` is the bug's CURRENT position, which may not lie on the line from `Pprev` to `T`\n   382→- Locking an axis forces `P` onto the line, but does so instantly (snap), not smoothly\n   383→\n   384→**Example of geometric incorrectness:**\n   385→\n   386→```\n   387→Pprev = GridPosition(2, 3) → world (100, 140)\n   388→T = GridPosition(3, 3) → world (140, 140)\n   389→P_current = (118, 142)  // Bug is 2 pixels above the line\n   390→\n   391→gridDelta = (1, 0) → horizontal segment detected\n   392→Axis lock: P.y = T.y = 140  // SNAP from 142 → 140\n   393→Result: Bug visibly \"drops\" 2 pixels instantly\n   394→```\n   395→\n   396→**Correct approach (SMOOTH):**\n   397→\n   398→```\n   399→direction = normalize(T - P)  // Direction from current position to target\n   400→P += direction * speed * deltaTime  // Move toward target smoothly\n   401→```\n   402→\n   403→Using the same example:\n   404→```\n   405→P_current = (118, 142)\n   406→T = (140, 140)\n   407→delta = T - P = (22, -2)\n   408→distance = sqrt(22² + 2²) = sqrt(488) ≈ 22.09\n   409→direction = (22/22.09, -2/22.09) ≈ (0.995, -0.091)\n   410→\n   411→If speed * deltaTime = 5:\n   412→P_next = P + direction * 5 = (118 + 4.975, 142 - 0.455) = (122.975, 141.545)\n   413→\n   414→Next frame:\n   415→delta = (140, 140) - (122.975, 141.545) = (17.025, -1.545)\n   416→distance ≈ 17.09\n   417→direction ≈ (0.996, -0.090)\n   418→P_next = (122.975 + 4.98, 141.545 - 0.45) = (127.955, 141.095)\n   419→\n   420→... bug smoothly moves toward (140, 140) in both X and Y simultaneously\n   421→```\n   422→\n   423→**Key insight:** The correct approach calculates direction from CURRENT position, not from previous waypoint. This ensures smooth movement even when bug is off-path.\n   424→\n   425→### Why Axis Locks Fail on Curves\n   426→\n   427→**At a corner waypoint:**\n   428→\n   429→```\n   430→Path: [..., (2,3), (3,3), (3,4), ...]\n   431→                  corner\n   432→\n   433→Bug approaching (3,3) horizontally from (2,3):\n   434→  - Horizontal branch active: Y locked to 140 (y-coordinate of row 3)\n   435→  - Bug reaches (3,3), pathIndex increments to target (3,4)\n   436→\n   437→Bug now targeting (3,4) vertically:\n   438→  - Vertical branch activates: X locked to 140 (x-coordinate of column 3)\n   439→  - IF bug.x was already 140 → smooth transition ✓\n   440→  - IF bug.x was 139.5 due to timing → SNAP to 140 ✗ (visible jerk)\n   441→```\n   442→\n   443→**The problem at corners:**\n   444→- Axis locks ASSUME perfect alignment at waypoint arrival\n   445→- The `distance < 2` check snaps position (line 282), which should fix this\n   446→- **BUT:** If bug doesn't trigger the snap (e.g., approaches waypoint at an angle due to previous drift), the axis lock on the NEW segment snaps BEFORE the waypoint is reached\n   447→\n   448→**Real-world corner scenario:**\n   449→\n   450→```\n   451→Frame N-2: Bug at (136, 138), target (140, 140) [horizontal segment]\n   452→           distance = 5.66, no snap, horizontal branch\n   453→           Y locked to 140 → position becomes (136, 140) [SNAP!]\n   454→           X moves toward 140 → position becomes (138, 140)\n   455→\n   456→Frame N-1: Bug at (138, 140), target (140, 140)\n   457→           distance = 2, no snap yet (≥ 2)\n   458→           Horizontal branch: Y=140 ✓, X moves → (140, 140)\n   459→\n   460→Frame N:   Bug at (140, 140), target (140, 140)\n   461→           distance = 0 < 2 → SNAP to (140, 140), pathIndex++\n   462→\n   463→Frame N+1: Bug at (140, 140), target (140, 180) [vertical segment]\n   464→           distance = 40\n   465→           Vertical branch: X locked to 140 ✓ (already aligned)\n   466→           Y moves toward 180 → (140, 142)\n   467→```\n   468→\n   469→In this scenario, the system worked because the snap happened before the corner. But if Frame N-2 had bug at (136, 141) instead of (136, 138):\n   470→\n   471→```\n   472→Frame N-2: Bug at (136, 141), target (140, 140)\n   473→           Horizontal branch: Y locked to 140 → (136, 140) [SNAP from 141!]\n   474→```\n   475→\n   476→The snap is visible as a 1-pixel \"jerk\" downward. Multiple such snaps across a path create the \"drifting off road\" visual effect.\n   477→\n   478→## Recommended Solution\n   479→\n   480→### Vector-Based Movement (Hero.swift Pattern)\n   481→\n   482→**Replace lines 292-314 with:**\n   483→\n   484→```swift\n   485→// Calculate direction and move toward target\n   486→let moveDistance = moveSpeed * slowFactor * CGFloat(deltaTime)\n   487→\n   488→// Always move directly toward target using normalized direction\n   489→// (Following pattern from Hero.swift:110-127)\n   490→let ratio = min(1.0, moveDistance / distance)\n   491→position.x += dx * ratio\n   492→position.y += dy * ratio\n   493→\n   494→// Note: gridPosition will be updated when waypoint is reached (line 283)\n   495→```\n   496→\n   497→### Why This Approach Is Correct\n   498→\n   499→**1. Geometric correctness:**\n   500→- Direction vector `(dx, dy)` points from current position to target\n   501→- Normalization via `ratio = moveDistance / distance` ensures speed is constant\n   502→- Bug ALWAYS moves directly toward target, regardless of path shape\n   503→\n   504→**2. Handles all path types:**\n   505→- Horizontal segments: `dy ≈ 0`, so `ratio * dy ≈ 0`, Y changes minimally ✓\n   506→- Vertical segments: `dx ≈ 0`, so `ratio * dx ≈ 0`, X changes minimally ✓\n   507→- Diagonal segments: Both `dx` and `dy` non-zero, both update proportionally ✓\n   508→- Curved paths: Direction recalculates each frame based on CURRENT position ✓\n   509→\n   510→**3. No axis assumptions:**\n   511→- Never assumes bug is already aligned with any axis\n   512→- Works even if bug is off-path due to previous errors\n   513→- Naturally corrects position errors over time\n   514→\n   515→**4. Mathematical equivalence to normalization:**\n   516→\n   517→The ratio approach: `position += delta * (moveDistance / distance)`\n   518→\n   519→Is equivalent to: `position += normalize(delta) * moveDistance`\n   520→\n   521→Because: `normalize(delta) = delta / distance`\n   522→\n   523→Therefore: `delta * (moveDistance / distance) = normalize(delta) * moveDistance` ✓\n   524→\n   525→**5. Proven pattern:**\n   526→\n   527→From `Hero.swift:110-127`:\n   528→```swift\n   529→let dx = targetWorldPos.x - position.x\n   530→let dy = targetWorldPos.y - position.y\n   531→let distance = sqrt(dx * dx + dy * dy)\n   532→\n   533→if distance < 5.0 {\n   534→    position = targetWorldPos\n   535→    currentGridPosition = target\n   536→    targetPosition = nil\n   537→} else {\n   538→    let moveDistance = moveSpeed * CGFloat(deltaTime)\n   539→    let ratio = min(1.0, moveDistance / distance)\n   540→    position.x += dx * ratio\n   541→    position.y += dy * ratio\n   542→}\n   543→```\n   544→\n   545→Hero movement is smooth and doesn't drift. Same logic should apply to bugs.\n   546→\n   547→### What to Preserve\n   548→\n   549→**Keep unchanged:**\n   550→- Lines 255-270: Guard check and burrowing logic (unrelated to drift)\n   551→- Lines 272-278: Target waypoint and distance calculation (correct)\n   552→- Lines 280-285: Waypoint snap logic (prevents division by zero, ensures exact positioning at waypoints)\n   553→\n   554→**Remove entirely:**\n   555→- Lines 292-296: Segment direction detection from grid deltas\n   556→- Lines 297-314: Three-branch movement logic (diagonal/horizontal/vertical)\n   557→\n   558→**Result:** Simpler, more maintainable code that is geometrically correct.\n   559→\n   560→### Performance Considerations\n   561→\n   562→**Computational complexity:** O(1) per frame per bug (same as current)\n   563→\n   564→**Operations comparison:**\n   565→\n   566→Current approach:\n   567→- 2x grid position lookups\n   568→- 2x abs() calls (deltaX, deltaY)\n   569→- 2-3 comparisons for branching\n   570→- 1x sqrt() for distance\n   571→- 2-3 arithmetic operations per branch\n   572→- **Total: ~10-12 operations**\n   573→\n   574→Proposed approach:\n   575→- 1x sqrt() for distance\n   576→- 3x divisions (ratio calculation, implicit in multiplication)\n   577→- 2x additions for position update\n   578→- **Total: ~6 operations**\n   579→\n   580→**Proposed approach is actually SIMPLER and potentially faster!**\n   581→\n   582→No performance concerns. The sqrt() call was already present (line 278), so no new overhead.\n   583→\n   584→## Test Scenarios for Implementation (TASK1)\n   585→\n   586→### Unit Tests (Tests/BugDefenseTests/)\n   587→\n   588→**Test framework:** XCTest\n   589→**Test command:** `swift test`\n   590→**Pattern:** Follow `BugDefenseTests.swift:1-100` for structure\n   591→\n   592→#### 1. vector math used in all game engines\n   158→\n   159→**Alternative approaches considered:**\n   160→- Tile-by-tile snapping: Would work but creates jerky movement\n   161→- Bezier curves: Overkill for straight tile-to-tile movement\n   162→- State machine for segment types: More complex than needed, prone to same heuristic errors\n   163→\n   164→**Trade-offs:**\n   165→- **Chosen:** Vector 1]\n   240→        let end = waypoints[i]\n   241→        let dx = end.x - start.x\n   242→        let dy = end.y - start.y\n   243→        let steps = max(abs(dx), abs(dy))  // Correctly handles orthogonal and diagonal\n   244→\n   245→        if steps == 0 { continue }\n   246→\n   247→        for step in 1...steps {\n   248→            let x = start.x + (dx * step) / steps  // Linear interpolation\n   249→            let y = start.y + (dy * step) / steps\n   250→            let position = GridPosition(x: x, y: y)\n   251→            if position != expandedPath.last {\n   252→                expandedPath.append(position)\n   253→            }\n   254→        }\n   255→    }\n   256→    return expandedPath\n   257→}\n   258→```\n   259→\n   260→**Verification Result: PATH SYSTEM IS CORRECT**\n   261→\n   262→- Uses `max(abs(dx), abs(dy))` to calculate steps -
